espn-604015.headline: Argentina want Cordoba back, with 16 points of interest
beats: Scotland won 47–38 in Cordoba in July, on the Nations Championship's opening round. The rematch is the seventh-place final at Twickenham, and Felipe Contepomi's side arrive wanting that one back.
They arrive leaking. Argentina conceded 42 at Ireland and 45 at France this month. Scotland put 67 past Japan on 21 November with a side that has since been mostly replaced.

Gregor Townsend makes 11 changes and is back to full strength. Rory Darge returns from a shoulder injury to captain in place of the injured Sione Tuipulotu, with Finn Russell back at 10. Contepomi benched Zebre's Tobias Wade, uncapped, ahead of Matias Moroni, who would have won his 100th cap.
Win by 16 or more and Argentina go above Scotland into sixth in the world. In Cordoba the margin was nine, the other way.

espn-604016.headline: Two points in Paris, six matches for Erasmus
beats: On 13 November France led 21-7 on three first-half tries, then hung on as the South African scrum took over. They conceded 14 penalties and three yellow cards, and held out a last attack from halfway to win 21-19.

Rassie Erasmus then claimed the officials missed 17 French knee-drop tackles and asked whether that was "match-fixing". It cost him a six-match ban. Without him, South Africa lost 20-17 to Ireland, their first back-to-back defeats since 2022.

Galthié has met the scrum problem with an all-Bordeaux-Bègles front row, holding Gros and Mauvaka back for the last half-hour. He also has Thomas Ramos again, out with a thigh problem since September.
Win again and France take first place in the world rankings from South Africa. Erasmus will not be in the building to dispute it.
